Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

Title: Diagnosis of test `shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries`

Details: The test `shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries` expects an `IOException` when reading a truncated tar archive. It reads entries with `getNextTarEntry()` and copies their content using `IOUtils.copy()`. The failure suggests an exception is not thrown as expected.

Analyzing `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()`, it reads header blocks and creates `TarArchiveEntry` objects, handling special entries like GNU long names and sparse files. For sparse files, `readGNUSparse()` reads additional sparse headers, and in `getLongNameData()` it reads entire long name data, detects malformed archives (returns null for malformed long name entries).

The `read()` method reads entry content from the underlying stream, respecting `entrySize` and `entryOffset`. It returns -1 if EOF or entry fully read. The test likely expects an IOException on truncated entry data, but the current logic in `read()` and `getNextTarEntry()` may not detect truncation properly.

`read()` relies on `is.read()`, which might not raise errors even if data is truncated, simply returning fewer bytes or -1 (EOF). No explicit validation of expected entry size after reading occurs in `getNextTarEntry()`. Hence, truncated entries might be silently accepted.

This absence of strict truncated data detection causes the test expecting an IOException to fail, as the truncated entry is read without error.

Best locations to fix:
- `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()`
- `TarArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
